title: Whoopi Goldberg’s Life in Photos, from Young Comedian to EGOT-Winning Legend, in Honor of Her 71st Birthday
text:

 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to homepage Whoopi Goldberg’s Life in Photos, from Young Comedian to EGOT-Winning Legend, in Honor of Her 71st Birthday
 At 71 years old, Goldberg is part of a select few entertainers who’ve earned an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony Award
 Stephanie Sengwe Fri, 13 November 2026 at 11:00 am UTC 6 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Whoopi Goldberg
Credit: Bonnie Schiffman/Getty Whoopi Goldberg is 71!
 Born on Nov. 13, 1955 in New York, Goldberg got her start as a comedian, performing in improv groups before gaining notoriety for her one-woman show. She scored the role of Celie in The Color Purple back in 1985, which launched her career as a serious actress as well. Goldberg would eventually get the coveted EGOT (an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony Award) for her incredible work.
 In her personal life, Goldberg shares a daughter, Alex Martin, with her first husband Alvin Martin. And though she would be married two more times following their divorce in 1979, she later admitted to realizing marriage wasn't for her , famously telling The New York Times, "I'm much happier on my own. I can spend as much time with somebody as I want to spend, but I'm not looking to be with somebody forever or live with someone."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement She added, "I don't want somebody in my house."
 As the screen legend marks her 71st birthday today, look back at her incredible life in photos.
 01 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg's Early Days
 Whoopi Goldberg 
 Credit: Nancy R. Schiff/Getty 
 Whoopi Goldberg was born Caryn Elaine Johnson in Manhattan, New York to Emma Harris, a teacher and Robert James Johnson Jr., a Baptist clergyman. ( See some of her cutest baby pics here. )
 02 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg Becomes a Mother
 Whoopi Goldberg and Alex Martin 
 Credit: Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection via Getty 
 Whoopi Goldberg married her first husband, Alvin Martin in 1973. Martin had been her drug counselor , as the actress was battling addiction at the time. They welcomed their only daughter, Alexandrea (pictured with her mom in 1993) that same year, and eventually divorced six years later in 1979.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 03 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg Goes West
 Whoopi Goldberg 
 Credit: Bonnie Schiffman/Getty 
 After training under Uta Hagen in the early '80s, Johnson moved to the West Coast, where she worked with improv groups and honed her skills as a comedian. Around the same time, she began garnering attention for her work portraying Moms Mabley in a one-woman show.
 By this point, she had changed her name into the one she's known for today, for one very specific reason.
 "Here's the thing. When you're performing on stage, you never really have time to go into the bathroom and close the door. So if you get a little gassy, you've got to let it go. So people used to say to me, 'You are like a whoopee cushion.' And that's where the name came from," she told the New York Times in 2006 .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The actress revealed that her stage moniker was initially Whoopie Cushión (yes, with a little French flair). However, her mother told her no one would take her seriously, and recommended she pick a surname with more meaning, she said on Late Night with Seth Meyers. 
 "[My mother] said, 'Well, there's a lot of family names, we've got a lot of different people in our family, I like Goldberg.' And I said, 'Okay well we'll try it.'"
 04 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg and Friends
 Billy Crystal, Whoopi Goldberg and Robin Williams 
 Credit: Bob Riha Jr./Getty 
 Above, the actress is pictured on stage with Billy Crystal and Robin Williams as they perform during a Comic Relief fundraising concert in 1986.
 05 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg Wins a Grammy
 Whoopi Goldberg 
 Credit: Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty 
 Goldberg took her first step into EGOT status back in 1986, when she made history as the first Black woman to win Best Comedy Recording for Whoopi Goldberg: Direct from Broadway, the recording of her one-woman show.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 06 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg Breaks Through
 Whoopi Goldberg 
 Credit: Warner Brothers/Getty 
 In 1985, Goldberg made her major acting debut, playing Celie in Steven Spielberg's The Color Purple. The film scored a whopping 11 Academy Award nominations, including Best Actress in a Leading Role for Goldberg.
 07 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg Wins a Golden Globe
 Whoopi Goldberg 
 Credit: Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty 
 Though she lost out at the Oscars, she took home the gold at the Golden Globes, snagging the trophy for Best Performance by an Actress in a Motion Picture — Drama.
 08 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg Stars in 'Ghost'
 Whoopi Goldberg and Patrick Swayze 
 Credit: CBS via Getty 
 In 1990, Goldberg hit box office gold again, starring in Ghost alongside Patrick Swayze, Demi Moore and Tony Goldwyn. The film would score her another Golden Globe, this time for Best Performance by an Actress in a Supporting Role.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 09 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg Wins an Oscar
 Whoopi Goldberg 
 Credit: Bettmann Archive/Getty 
 She also won big at the Oscars that year, taking home the statue for Best Supporting Actress.
 10 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg in 'Sister Act'
 Whoopi Goldberg 
 Credit: Suzanne Hanover/Buena Vista Pictures 
 In 1992, Goldberg landed yet another hit, playing nightclub-singer-turned-Catholic-sister in Sister Act. She earned another Golden Globe nod and the film would get a sequel the following year. (She recently said she'd like to do a third!)
 11 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg, the EGOT
 Mary Tyler Moore and Whoopi Goldberg 
 Credit: Scott Gries/ImageDirect via Getty 
 In 2002, the powerhouse actress officially became an EGOT, winning a Tony for her work as a producer on Thoroughly Modern Millie. That same year, she also won an Emmy for hosting Beyond Tara: The Extraordinary Life of Hattie McDaniel. 
 12 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg Joins 'The View'
 Whoopi Goldberg, Barbara Walters, Joy Behar, Sherri Shepherd, and Elisabeth Hasselbeck 
 Credit: Jeffrey Neira/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ever-opinionated, Goldberg joined The View as a host in 2007, following Rosie O'Donnell's departure. She would garner a Daytime Emmy for Outstanding Talk Show Host in 2009.
 13 of 14
 Whoopi Goldberg's Early Works Get Revived
 Whoopi Goldberg and Kerry Washington 
 Credit: Bruce Glikas/WireImage 
 In the summer of 2026, Kerry Washington produced and starred in The Whoopi Monologues , revisiting Goldberg's hit one-woman show. In addition to Washington, the production also featured Dominique Fishback, Kecia Lewis, Danielle Pinnock, Kara Young and Jurnee Smollet.
 14 of 14
 Whoopi Golberg, the GOAT
 Whoopi Goldberg and Alex Martin 
 Credit: Kelsey McNeal/Disney via Getty 
 These days, Goldberg continues to work steadily as an actor, producer and entertainment exec ( she helped launch the All Womens' Sports Network ), lending her talents to Till, Harlem , The Godfather of Harlem, and Hacks, while still hosting The View . In 2011, the actress also revealed she became a great-grandmother while on The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon.
